title: Chaplin, two reels at a time
blurb: The shorts Chaplin made between 1914 and 1917, when he went from a Keystone bit player to the most famous face on earth. Twenty minutes each. Start with The Immigrant if you only watch one.

films.note: The boat, the coin, the restaurant. Chaplin said it touched him more than anything else he made.
The alarm clock scene. He takes it apart like a surgeon and pronounces it dead.
One man, one house, one drink too many. Chaplin alone on screen for twenty minutes.
Chaplin on roller skates. He really could.
An escaped convict crashes a society party. The ice-cream-down-the-dress gag.
The first Mutual short, and the first escalator chase in film.
A tailor's assistant impersonates a count at a dinner. The spaghetti.
His first film for Essanay, set in a film studio. Gloria Swanson is an extra.
Chaplin plays two drunks in the same theatre, one in the stalls and one in the gallery.
Press-ganged onto a ship. The rolling-deck gags were done with a real tilting set.
Six minutes. The first time anyone saw the Tramp. He is ruining a newsreel.
The first feature-length comedy ever made, with Marie Dressler. Chaplin is the villain.
